title: Case Assignment Fairness and SLA Control Tower
subtitle: ClearPath Case Services (fictional) · 15,908 cases · 2 January to 30 June 2026. Leadership asked which team was underperforming. Workload per analyst hour is near-equal across all five teams, yet SLA compliance ranges from 26% to 84%. The cause is a target and a routing method, not a team.
limitations: Reassignment is treated as a routing failure, which overstates it because no reason code separates misroutes from legitimate escalations. SLA is measured in elapsed clock hours, not business hours, because the source has no business calendar. The complexity score weights are analyst judgement and were not fitted to outcomes. The data is fully synthetic, so the relationships shown here were built into the generator — what transfers is the method, not the conclusion.
footer: Source: synthetic data generated by src/generate_data.py, seed 8821. No employer data, patient information, protected health information or confidential business information is used. Analyst performance is reported by tenure band only, never by individual.

queries.headline: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_cases, SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS resolved, SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status<>'Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_cases, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met_Calculated='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS accuracy_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reopened_Flag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS reopen_pct, ROUND(AVG(Resolution_Hours),1) AS avg_hours, ROUND(SUM(SLA_Breach_Hours),0) AS breach_hours FROM case_data
queries.dq: SELECT COUNT(*) AS exceptions, SUM(CASE WHEN Action_Taken='Excluded from reporting' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS excluded, ROUND(100.0*(1.0-1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Action_Taken='Excluded from reporting' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/16055),2) AS dq_score FROM dq_exceptions
queries.by_case_type: SELECT Case_Type, MAX(SLA_Target_Hours) AS target_hours, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met_Calculated='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(AVG(Resolution_Hours),1) AS avg_hours, ROUND(SUM(SLA_Breach_Hours),0) AS breach_hours FROM case_data GROUP BY Case_Type ORDER BY sla_pct
queries.teams: SELECT w.Team_ID, t.Primary_Capability, w.Analyst_Count, w.Cases_Handled, ROUND(w.Avg_Complexity,1) AS avg_complexity, w.Workload_Balance_Index, w.Balance_Status, w.SLA_Compliance_Pct, w.Assignment_Accuracy_Pct, w.Median_Resolution_Hours FROM team_workload w JOIN dim_team t ON t.Team_ID=w.Team_ID ORDER BY w.SLA_Compliance_Pct
queries.routing: SELECT Routing_Method, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS accuracy_pct, ROUND(AVG(Assignment_Lag_Hours),2) AS lag_hours, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reopened_Flag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS reopen_pct FROM case_data GROUP BY Routing_Method ORDER BY accuracy_pct DESC
queries.reassign_cost: SELECT CAST(Reassignment_Count AS INT) AS reassignments, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(AVG(Resolution_Hours),1) AS avg_hours, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met_Calculated='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reopened_Flag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS reopen_pct FROM case_data WHERE Reassignment_Count IS NOT NULL AND Reassignment_Count<=3 GROUP BY reassignments ORDER BY reassignments
queries.complexity: SELECT Complexity_Band, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met_Calculated='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS reassigned_pct FROM case_data GROUP BY Complexity_Band ORDER BY AVG(Complexity_Score)
queries.equity_scatter: SELECT Team_ID, Workload_Balance_Index AS wbi, SLA_Compliance_Pct AS sla_pct FROM team_workload
queries.backlog: SELECT Team_ID, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN Available_Hours>0 THEN Backlog_Work_Hours/Available_Hours END),2) AS backlog_days FROM team_capacity GROUP BY Team_ID ORDER BY backlog_days DESC
queries.root_cause: SELECT Root_Cause, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(AVG(Resolution_Hours),1) AS avg_hours, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reopened_Flag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS reopen_pct FROM case_data WHERE Current_Status='Resolved' GROUP BY Root_Cause ORDER BY cases DESC
queries.monthly: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', Created_Date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met_Calculated='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Reassignment_Count IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS accuracy_pct FROM case_data GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
queries.tenure: SELECT a.Tenure_Band AS tenure, COUNT(c.Case_ID) AS cases, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN c.SLA_Met_Calculated='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN c.Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct FROM dim_analyst a JOIN case_data c ON c.Assigned_Analyst=a.Analyst_ID GROUP BY a.Tenure_Band ORDER BY a.Tenure_Band
queries.segment: SELECT Customer_Segment AS segment, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met_Calculated='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Current_Status='Resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct FROM case_data GROUP BY Customer_Segment ORDER BY sla_pct
queries.queue: SELECT Case_ID, Case_Type, Priority, Assigned_Team, Complexity_Band, Current_Status, ROUND((julianday('2026-06-30')-julianday(Created_Date))*24-SLA_Target_Hours,1) AS past_target FROM case_data WHERE Current_Status<>'Resolved' ORDER BY past_target DESC, Complexity_Score DESC LIMIT 25
queries.exceptions: SELECT Rule_ID, Severity, Action_Taken, COUNT(*) AS exceptions FROM dq_exceptions GROUP BY Rule_ID, Severity, Action_Taken ORDER BY exceptions DESC

cards.title: SLA compliance by case type, against its own target
cards.desc: The dashed line is the blended 62.70% figure reported to clients. Two case types sit far below it, and they are the only two whose average resolution time exceeds their own target.

cards.title: Where the lateness actually is
cards.desc: Total breach hours by case type. Authorization Review is 41% of all lateness from 14% of cases.

cards.title: Average resolution time vs the published target
cards.desc: Authorization Review takes 79.0 hours against a 48-hour target. Enrollment Change takes 30.9 against 24. No amount of coaching closes a target set below the time the work takes.

cards.title: Workload balance vs outcome
cards.desc: One point per team. If workload explained the SLA spread these would form a line. They do not.

cards.title: Team equity — the index alongside the outcomes
cards.desc: The only team flagged Overloaded has the second-best SLA. The worst SLA sits inside the Balanced band. Assignment accuracy varies by just 1.6 points across all five teams, so this is not analyst skill.

cards.title: Routing accuracy by method
cards.desc: Auto-routing carries 58% of volume at the worst accuracy. Manual triage is 17.1 points better and reopens less, paying only 2.2 extra hours of assignment lag for it.

cards.title: What a reassignment costs
cards.desc: One reassignment adds 20.8 hours, drops SLA compliance 26 points and nearly triples the reopen rate. Bars are case counts on the right axis.

cards.title: Does the complexity score predict anything?
cards.desc: Monotonic in the right direction across all four bands, which is the most that can be claimed for weights assigned by judgement rather than fitted to outcomes. The gradient is too shallow to use as a routing rule on its own.

cards.title: Backlog days of work
cards.desc: Backlog work hours divided by available hours. This is the queue-time dimension the Workload Balance Index misses, and it is where TEAM-04's problem becomes visible.

cards.title: Root cause of resolved cases
cards.desc: Missing documentation is the largest single cause at 26.0% of resolved volume. It is found after assignment, when the case is already on the clock.

cards.title: Monthly trend
cards.desc: Six flat months. Two coaching cycles were spent in this window with no visible effect, which is the evidence that the intervention was aimed at the wrong thing.

cards.title: Tenure effect — real but small
cards.desc: An 8.2 point gap between newest and most experienced analysts. Worth onboarding attention; nowhere near enough to explain a 58 point team gap.

cards.title: Segment equity — a null finding, reported anyway
cards.desc: Tested for favouritism toward larger clients and found none: a 1.3 point spread across four segments on materially identical average complexity.

cards.title: Priority queue — open cases ranked for action
cards.desc: Sorted by hours past target, then complexity. Deliberately not sorted by priority, which would bury a Low-priority case 112 hours late beneath an Urgent case with headroom left.

cards.title: Data quality exception log
cards.desc: Every rule violation, its severity and what was done about it. Critical failures are excluded and logged, never silently corrected — 34 cases marked Resolved with no resolution date could not be given a date without fabricating the SLA outcome being measured.
